chapter: Family and boyhood in Concord and Ione
title: The family home in Concord and the Clayton ranch
summary: The house in town behind the Presbyterian Church where his mother directed the choir, versus the ranch near today's Concord Pavilion where he almost learned to drive.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What was your home like in Concord? I know when you moved to Ione, you lived on a large ranch.
In Concord were you in a city? Or was that like a ranch too?

Part of our lot, at the back of the house, faced Main Street, behind the Presbyterian Church, where my mother was choir director 17 years. Then this house that I was born in was the Ivy House, from her father. She might have been born in the house, I’ve heard. She might have been born on a farm near the statue that’s between Walnut Creek and Pacheco. [ ] a statue.
So there was a house that was in town.
The ranch? Oh, that was in a different little town, Clayton.
If you know where the Concord Pavilion is, my dad used to run cattle on that very land. Then on up that hill was another ranch that I went to a lot when I was a kid.
But you didn’t live on the ranch. You lived in a home in town, and the ranch was out in Clayton.

Yeah. Right by the Pavilion. I often would think of that when I’d go to play a concert. This is the road I learn to drive – or almost learned to drive a car on. I ran through an orchard, my dad hollering, “Step on the other one!” I put my foot on the clutch instead of the brake. Went tearing through there.
